newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Put selling presses T-bond volatility.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Put selling presses T-bond volatility.

text.p: Implied volatility rates for U.S. Treasury bond options edged lower, under pressure from a bout of put selling in an otherwise quiet session that saw underlying futures hold to slim ranges.
The covered put sales, concentrated in the May 107 and 108 strikes, trimmed volatilities from slightly elevated opening levels, options traders said.

Two separate desks sold a total of 2,000 May 107 puts and 500 May 108 puts when the June bond futures contract was trading at 108-24. The 107 puts were sold at a premium of 28/64, with the 108 options going for 48/64.
Selling covered options is considered a pure volatility play. In the otherwise quiet market, the effect of the put sales on volatility was quickly felt, said a bond options trader.

May volatility dipped to 9.2 percent after opening at about 9.35 percent. On Friday, May settled at 9.0 percent. June edged down to 9.4 percent from 9.45 percent on the opening, up slightly from Friday's closing level.
May and June calls attracted some buying interest during the slow day. A dealer firm's purchase of 2,000 May 113 calls at a premium of 4/64 was one of the larger transactions.

Although market sentiment currently favors a short-term rate hike, options volatility should remain underpinned until the Federal Open Market Committee's decision on short-term interest rates is made known late in Tuesday's trading session, analysts on the bond floor said.
Then "as soon as it's official, they'll sell it, no matter what," the bond options trader predicted.
Activity in Eurodollar options was likewise subdued on the eve of the U.S. central bank's policy meeting. "Everybody's sitting and waiting for the results tomorrow," said a Eurodollar options trader.
One firm's sale of 500 short-dated April 93.25/93.50 put spreads, done at a premium of 11 basis points, was a highlight.

Eurodollar volatility was little changed on the day, with June estimated late in the session at 10.0 percent, September at 12.5 percent, December at 13.8 percent, March at 15.4 percent and June 1998 at 16.6 percent.
Vols for short-dated June and September options were estimated at 17.3 percent.
